featured_reviews.review_text:
Complaint number 1322.
Extremely disappointed with the quality and after-sales experience at Homes To Life, Juhu.

I purchased a recliner sofa from this store in April 2025 with the expectation that a premium-priced product would last for years. Shockingly, within just 13 months, the fabric has already started peeling off badly. This is completely unacceptable for furniture marketed as high quality.

A sofa is not a disposable product. Normal wear and tear is expected after 5–7 years, not barely one year after purchase. This clearly reflects either substandard material quality or poor manufacturing standards.

This is not the quality one expects from a so-called premium furniture brand in Juhu. Leadership seriously needs to investigate:

- Quality of fabric being used
- Vendor/manufacturing standards
- Misleading sales commitments who will not pick up calls once sale is done
- Poor customer resolution process

A premium sofa peeling within 13 months is not “wear and tear” — it is product failure.

Instead of acknowledging a product that started deteriorating within just 13 months, the discussion quickly shifted toward finding reasons why the customer might be at fault. Rather than focusing on a solution, I was presented with vague explanations, excuses, and theories that seemed designed to defend the product rather than understand the problem.
They offered to change cover for 20k, so again I need to pay 20k in 1 years time when peeling starts again?
Quite rigid policy driven that only 12 months is under warranty, so 1 - 2 extra months buffer makes difference? Keeping aside reputation and ignoring future sales prospects. Attached photos speaking louder than marketing brochure under showroom lights.

Buyers are advised to verify all specifications, especially the motor brand, before making a purchase.
